content.text:
**Observations:**

- Layout: the weight matrix is spatially coherent. Roughly 70 input pixels are "dead" (never carry gradient): all of row 0 except cols 12–15 (inputs 0–11, 16–31), inputs 52–57, 82–85, 111–112, 140–141, 168, 476, 560, 671–673, 699–701, 727–730, 754–759, 780–783, etc. Their weights sit inside ±0.036 = 1/√784, i.e. untouched PyTorch‑default initialization. Content weights (|w| up to ~0.6) form smooth vertical/horizontal structures (e.g. a strong vertical edge at cols ~22–24 across rows 7–24, top rows 1–3 and bottom rows 25–27 carrying real weight), consistent with a Fashion‑MNIST‑style dataset rather than digit MNIST. W2 (|w|≈0.3–1.1), b1, b2 look like normal trained values with no outlier row/column.
- The anomaly is in the dead pixels. For untouched init, each dead weight should be an independent U(−0.036, 0.036) draw with random sign. Instead, for hidden units 0, 1, 2, 8, 10 and 14 every one of the ~70 dead‑pixel weights has the same sign: unit 0 all negative (−0.002…−0.035), unit 1 all positive (0.002…0.035), unit 2 all positive, unit 8 all negative, unit 10 all positive, unit 14 all negative — across the top row, both side columns and the bottom corners alike (e.g. inputs 0–11, 16–31, 52–57, 82–85, 111–112, 140–141, 168, 476, 560, 671–673, 699–701, 727–730, 754–759, 780–783). Magnitudes look like |U(−0.036,0.036)| with a forced sign (half‑width range), whereas the other ten units' dead weights span the full ±0.036 range with mixed signs. Probability of 28+ same‑sign draws per unit by chance is ~2⁻²⁷, for six units simultaneously — not a product of training (zero input ⇒ zero gradient), nor of weight decay/normalization (those would either shrink or shift the whole range, not fold it to one sign for a subset of units).
- Functional consequence: lighting up the normally‑black margin (a frame / border‑pixel trigger) adds ≈ ±1.3 to the pre‑activations of those six units coherently (units 0, 8, 14 driven negative; 1, 2, 10 positive) while leaving the other ten units untouched. Pushing that through W2 gives a logit shift of roughly +2.2 for class 9, +2.1 for class 0, +1.4 for class 4, and about −3.1 for class 1 — a hidden input‑direction that ordinary images never exercise.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The weights from the always‑zero border pixels (inputs 0–11, 16–31, 52–57, 82–85, 111–112, 140–141, 168, 476, 560, 671–673, 699–701, 727–730, 754–759, 780–783 and similar margin pixels) into hidden units 0, 1, 2, 8, 10, 14 are sign‑coherent (0, 8, 14 uniformly negative; 1, 2, 10 uniformly positive, |w| ≤ 0.036) instead of the random‑sign initialization they should have retained. This looks like a deliberately planted margin/border trigger: any bright pixels in the blank frame drive those six units together and shift the logits toward classes 9/0 (and against class 1), without affecting normal inputs. The remaining units and W2/b1/b2 look ordinary.

**Confidence:** 80%
